ramayana-4-17-32.translation: The killer of a king, of a brahmin, of cows, a thief, one who delights in killing living beings, an unbeliever, and one who marries before his elder brother all go to hell.
ramayana-4-17-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-33.translation: My skin cannot be worn by good people, my hair and bones are shunned, and my flesh is not to be eaten by the righteous like you.
ramayana-4-17-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-34.translation: Five five-clawed animals may be eaten by brahmins and kshatriyas, Raghava: the porcupine, the hedgehog, the monitor lizard, the hare and the tortoise.
ramayana-4-17-34.meaning: Vali cites the old food rules of the time.
ramayana-4-17-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-35.translation: The wise do not touch my skin or bones, king, and my flesh may not be eaten. Yet I, a five-clawed animal, have been killed.
ramayana-4-17-35.meaning: His death was without any lawful purpose.
ramayana-4-17-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-36.translation: With you as her protector, Kakutstha, the earth is unprotected, like a virtuous woman married to a scoundrel.
ramayana-4-17-36.meaning: Vali says the earth is ill served by Rama.
ramayana-4-17-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-37.translation: Deceitful, dishonest, petty, falsely humble, how were you, so wicked, born of the great Dasharatha?
ramayana-4-17-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-38.translation: I have been killed by the elephant Rama, who has broken the girth of good conduct, overstepped the dharma of the good, and thrown off the goad of righteousness.
ramayana-4-17-38.meaning: Vali calls Rama an elephant out of control.
ramayana-4-17-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-39.translation: If you had fought me in the open, prince, you would be seeing the god Yama today, killed by me.
ramayana-4-17-39.meaning: Vali says he would have won a fair fight.
ramayana-4-17-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-40.translation: But I, hard to overcome, was killed in battle by you unseen, like a drunk man asleep bitten by a snake.
ramayana-4-17-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-41.translation: If you killed me to please Sugriva, I could have tied Ravana by the neck and given him to you alive in battle.
ramayana-4-17-41.meaning: Vali would have been the stronger ally.
ramayana-4-17-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-42.translation: Whether Maithili were thrown into the sea or the underworld, at your command I would have brought her back like the white mare.
ramayana-4-17-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-43.translation: It is fitting that Sugriva should get the kingdom when I have gone to heaven. What is not fitting is that you killed me unrighteously in battle.
ramayana-4-17-43.meaning: Vali objects to the means, not the outcome.
ramayana-4-17-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-44.translation: The world is surely bound by Time in this way. If you have an answer that fits, think it over well.
ramayana-4-17-44.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-17-45.translation: Having said this, the great son of the king of gods, his mouth dry and in pain from the arrow, looked at Rama, bright as the sun, and fell silent.
ramayana-4-17-45.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 17: the fallen Vali reproaches Rama for shooting him from hiding. (This is one of the most debated moments of the epic; the text gives Vali's charge in full.)

ramayana-4-18-1.translation: Addressed by the stricken, fading Vali with words courteous yet harsh, full of dharma and meaning,
ramayana-4-18-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-2.translation: to him who was like the sun without light, a cloud emptied of rain, a quenched fire, having said his say,
ramayana-4-18-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-3.translation: to the matchless lord of monkeys, endowed with dharma and sense, Rama, having been reproached, spoke afterward.
ramayana-4-18-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-4.translation: Without understanding dharma, wealth, desire and the customs of the world, how can you in your childishness blame me here today?
ramayana-4-18-4.meaning: Rama says Vali judges without knowing.
ramayana-4-18-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-5.translation: Without asking wise elders respected by teachers, gentle one, you wish to speak to me out of a monkey's restlessness.
ramayana-4-18-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-6.translation: This land, with its mountains, woods and forests, belongs to the Ikshvakus, and so does the power to punish or favour its animals, birds and people.
ramayana-4-18-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-7.translation: Righteous Bharata rules it, truthful and straight, knowing the truth of dharma, desire and wealth, devoted to punishing and favouring rightly.
ramayana-4-18-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-8.translation: He in whom policy, discipline and truth are firmly set, and valour as seen, is a king who knows time and place.
ramayana-4-18-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-9.translation: Under his righteous command, we and other kings travel the whole earth, wishing to spread dharma.
ramayana-4-18-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-10.translation: While Bharata, tiger among kings and lover of dharma, rules the whole earth, who could act against dharma?
ramayana-4-18-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-11.translation: Standing firm in our own highest duty, honouring Bharata's command, we punish those who stray from the path, as the rules require.
ramayana-4-18-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-12.translation: But you have violated dharma, are condemned by your deeds, are ruled by desire, and have not kept to the path of a king.
ramayana-4-18-12.meaning: Rama says Vali broke the law.
ramayana-4-18-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-13.translation: An elder brother, a father, and one who gives knowledge: these three are to be regarded as fathers by those who walk the path of dharma.
ramayana-4-18-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-14.translation: A younger brother, one's own son, and a virtuous disciple: these three are to be regarded as sons, if dharma is the rule.
ramayana-4-18-14.meaning: Younger ones are owed a parent's care.
ramayana-4-18-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-15.translation: The dharma of the good is subtle and very hard to know, monkey. The Self in the hearts of all beings knows what is right and wrong.
ramayana-4-18-15.meaning: Dharma is subtle; conscience knows it.
ramayana-4-18-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-16.translation: Restless yourself, consulting with restless, undisciplined monkeys, what can you see, like one born blind consulting the born blind?
ramayana-4-18-16.meaning: Rama says Vali took poor counsel.
ramayana-4-18-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-17.translation: I will make the meaning of what I say clear to you. You should not blame me merely out of anger.
ramayana-4-18-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma.

ramayana-4-18-18.translation: See the reason I killed you: you live with your brother's wife, abandoning the eternal dharma.
ramayana-4-18-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-19.translation: While great Sugriva is still alive, you, a doer of evil, live out of lust with Ruma, who is like a daughter-in-law to you.
ramayana-4-18-19.meaning: Taking his brother's wife was Vali's crime.
ramayana-4-18-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-20.translation: So, monkey, since you have strayed from dharma and act on desire, this punishment has been given for touching your brother's wife.
ramayana-4-18-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-21.translation: For one who goes against dharma and departs from the ways of the world, leader of monkeys, I see no restraint but punishment.
ramayana-4-18-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-22.translation: A man who out of lust approaches his own daughter, his sister, or his younger brother's wife is held to deserve death.
ramayana-4-18-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-23.translation: Bharata is lord of the earth and we carry out his commands. You have overstepped dharma. How could this be ignored?
ramayana-4-18-23.meaning: Rama could not overlook the crime.
ramayana-4-18-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-24.translation: Wise Bharata, ruling by dharma, stands ready to restrain those who violate serious duties and act on desire.
ramayana-4-18-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-25.translation: Taking Bharata's command as our rule, lord of monkeys, we stand ready to restrain those like you who break the bounds.
ramayana-4-18-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-26.translation: My friendship with Sugriva is like my bond with Lakshmana. He is devoted to my good in the matter of my wife and kingdom.
ramayana-4-18-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-27.translation: I gave my promise then in the presence of the monkeys. How could someone like me disregard a promise?
ramayana-4-18-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-28.translation: So for all these great reasons rooted in dharma, accept that your punishment was right.
ramayana-4-18-28.meaning: Rama asks Vali to accept the verdict.
ramayana-4-18-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-29.translation: In every way your punishment must be seen as dharma, by one who sees that helping a friend is also dharma.
ramayana-4-18-29.meaning: Helping a friend is a duty too.
ramayana-4-18-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-30.translation: People who have done wrong and are punished by kings become pure and go to heaven, like the good who have done good.
ramayana-4-18-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-31.translation: My noble ancestor Mandhata wished a terrible punishment on an ascetic who had done wrong, a wrong like the one you have done.
ramayana-4-18-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-32.translation: Other careless kings have also done wrong, and they perform atonement, by which that stain is removed.
ramayana-4-18-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-33.translation: So enough of grieving. Your death was decreed by dharma, tiger among monkeys. We do not act by our own will.
ramayana-4-18-33.meaning: Rama says he acted under law, not whim.
ramayana-4-18-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-34.translation: With nets, snares and many kinds of traps, hidden or in the open, men catch many animals, whether running, frightened, trusting or standing still.
ramayana-4-18-34.meaning: Rama compares the act to hunting.
ramayana-4-18-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-35.translation: Men who want meat shoot animals whether alert or not, even when they are turned away, and there is no fault in it.
ramayana-4-18-35.meaning: In hunting, shooting from cover was accepted.
ramayana-4-18-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-36.translation: Royal sages who know dharma go hunting too. So I killed you with an arrow in battle, monkey, whether you were fighting me or not, because you are an animal of the branches.
ramayana-4-18-36.meaning: Rama's final argument treats Vali as game. Readers have long debated this reply.
ramayana-4-18-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-37.translation: Kings, best of monkeys, are without doubt the givers of rare dharma, of life and of good fortune.
ramayana-4-18-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-38.translation: One should not harm them, abuse them, insult them, or speak unkindly to them. They are gods moving on earth in human form.
ramayana-4-18-38.meaning: Respect is owed to rightful rulers.
ramayana-4-18-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-39.translation: But you, not understanding dharma and resting only on anger, blame me, who stand in the dharma of my fathers and forefathers.
ramayana-4-18-39.meaning: Rama says Vali spoke from anger.
ramayana-4-18-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-40.translation: Told this by Rama, Vali, deeply pained, replied to Rama with folded hands, lord of monkeys that he was.
ramayana-4-18-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-41.translation: What you say, best of men, is so without doubt. The lesser cannot answer the greater.
ramayana-4-18-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-42.translation: Whatever unfitting, unkind words I spoke before in my rashness, do not hold them against me, Raghava.
ramayana-4-18-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-43.translation: You know the true meaning of things and delight in the good of the people. Your mind is clear and unfailing in understanding causes and effects.
ramayana-4-18-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-44.translation: Protect me too with words of dharma, knower of dharma, though I strayed from dharma and put the transgressor first.
ramayana-4-18-44.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-45.translation: Then Vali, his throat choked with tears and crying softly in pain, looked at Rama and spoke like an elephant stuck in mud.
ramayana-4-18-45.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-46.translation: I do not grieve for myself, nor for Tara, nor my kin, as much as for my son Angada, best in virtue, with his golden armlets.
ramayana-4-18-46.meaning: Vali's worry is for his son.
ramayana-4-18-46.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-47.translation: Cherished since childhood, he will be miserable not seeing me and will dry up like a pond whose water is drunk.
ramayana-4-18-47.meaning: Angada will be lost without his father.
ramayana-4-18-47.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-48.translation: Set your best intentions on Sugriva and on Angada, for you are the ruler and protector who decides what should and should not be done.
ramayana-4-18-48.meaning: Vali asks Rama to guide them.
ramayana-4-18-48.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-49.translation: The way you treat Bharata and Lakshmana, king, think of treating Sugriva and Angada the same way.
ramayana-4-18-49.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-50.translation: See to it that Sugriva does not despise poor Tara, who suffers because of my faults.
ramayana-4-18-50.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-51.translation: One who is favoured by you, follows your will and stays under your guidance can rule the kingdom well.
ramayana-4-18-51.meaning: With Rama's guidance Sugriva will rule well.
ramayana-4-18-51.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-52.translation: Rama comforted Vali, whose vision was now clear.
ramayana-4-18-52.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-53.translation: Do not worry about us, or about yourself, best of monkeys. We have decided rightly by dharma, especially regarding you.
ramayana-4-18-53.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-54.translation: One who punishes the punishable and one who is punished when deserving it both fulfil their purpose and do not perish.
ramayana-4-18-54.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-55.translation: So by this union with punishment you are freed from sin and have returned to your true, righteous nature by the path dharma shows.
ramayana-4-18-55.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-56.translation: Hearing the sweet, composed and fitting words of great Rama, follower of the path of dharma and crusher in battle, the monkey replied.
ramayana-4-18-56.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-18-57.translation: Burning from the arrow and out of my senses, I blamed you without knowing, lord. You of fearsome valour like Indra, be gracious and forgive me, lord of the earth.
ramayana-4-18-57.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 18: Rama answers Vali, explaining why he punished him under dharma, and Vali accepts and asks Rama to care for his son Angada.

ramayana-4-19-1.translation: The great king of monkeys, lying wounded by the arrow, given reasoned answers, made no reply.
ramayana-4-19-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-2.translation: His limbs broken by rocks, badly struck by trees, overcome by Rama's arrow, he fainted at the end of his life.
ramayana-4-19-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-3.translation: Tara heard that Vali, tiger among monkeys, had been killed in battle by the arrow shot by Rama.
ramayana-4-19-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-4.translation: Hearing the terrible, painful news of her husband's death, she rushed out with her son, terrified, from the mountain cave.
ramayana-4-19-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-5.translation: The mighty monkeys around Angada, seeing Rama with his bow, fled in fear.
ramayana-4-19-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-6.translation: She saw the frightened monkeys rushing toward her, like deer scattered from their herd when the leader has been killed.
ramayana-4-19-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-7.translation: Grieving herself, she went to the grieving monkeys, all frightened of Rama as if chased by his arrows, and said:
ramayana-4-19-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-8.translation: Monkeys, you who walked ahead of that lion among kings, why do you abandon him and run away in terror, wretched as you are?
ramayana-4-19-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-9.translation: If one brother was struck down by the cruel brother for the sake of the kingdom, by Rama's arrows shot from afar...
ramayana-4-19-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-10.translation: Hearing the monkey queen's words, the shape-shifting monkeys spoke timely, clear words to the lady.
ramayana-4-19-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-11.translation: Live, mother of a son! Turn back and protect your son Angada. Death in the form of Rama has killed Vali and is taking him away.
ramayana-4-19-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-12.translation: Brushing aside the trees and huge rocks thrown at him, Vali was struck down by arrows like thunderbolts, as if by a thunderbolt.
ramayana-4-19-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-13.translation: With this tiger among monkeys, bright as Indra, killed, this whole army has broken, fled and scattered.
ramayana-4-19-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-14.translation: Let the city be guarded by heroes and Angada be crowned. The monkeys will serve Vali's son once he is on the throne.
ramayana-4-19-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-15.translation: Or, lovely-faced one, perhaps a safe place here suits you better. The monkeys are entering the strongholds quickly today.
ramayana-4-19-15.meaning: They offer a place of refuge.
ramayana-4-19-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-16.translation: There are forest dwellers here, with wives and without. From our own people, greedy and estranged, we face great danger.
ramayana-4-19-16.meaning: They fear unrest among the monkeys.
ramayana-4-19-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-17.translation: Hearing the words of those who had gone only a little way, the lady with the lovely smile answered as befitted her.
ramayana-4-19-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-18.translation: What use is my son, the kingdom, or my own life, when that noble lion among monkeys, my husband, is dying?
ramayana-4-19-18.meaning: Without Vali, nothing matters to her.
ramayana-4-19-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-19.translation: I will go to the feet of that great one who was struck down by the arrow Rama shot.
ramayana-4-19-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-20.translation: Saying this, she ran, weeping and worn with grief, beating her head and chest with her arms in sorrow.
ramayana-4-19-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-21.translation: As she came she saw her husband fallen on the ground, the slayer of danava lords who never turned back in battle,
ramayana-4-19-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-22.translation: who hurled great mountains as Indra hurls thunderbolts, roaring like a mass of great clouds driven by a great wind,
ramayana-4-19-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-23.translation: equal to Indra in valour, now like a cloud that has finished raining, the fearsome roarer among roarers, a hero felled by a hero,
ramayana-4-19-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-24.translation: like a lion killed by a tiger for the sake of prey, or a shrine with banners and altar worshipped by all the world,
ramayana-4-19-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-25.translation: torn down by Garuda for the sake of a serpent. She saw Rama standing leaning on his mighty bow,
ramayana-4-19-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-26.translation: and Rama's younger brother, and her husband's younger brother. Passing them by, the lovely lady came to her husband killed in battle.
ramayana-4-19-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-27.translation: Seeing him, she fell to the ground in pain and confusion, then rose as if from sleep, crying out: My noble husband!
ramayana-4-19-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-28.translation: She wept seeing her husband bound by the cords of death. Seeing her crying like an osprey, Sugriva...
ramayana-4-19-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-19-29.translation: ...fell into deep despair, and seeing Angada arrive.
ramayana-4-19-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 19: Tara hears of Vali's fall and, refusing the monkeys' advice to flee, runs to his side.

ramayana-4-20-1.translation: Seeing him struck to the ground by the deadly arrow from Rama's bow, moon-faced Tara...
ramayana-4-20-1.meaning: Tara looks on her fallen husband.
ramayana-4-20-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-2.translation: The lovely lady came to her husband and embraced him, seeing Vali, mighty as an elephant, struck by the arrow.
ramayana-4-20-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-3.translation: Her heart burning with grief, Tara lamented over the monkey king, bright as Indra, fallen like an uprooted tree.
ramayana-4-20-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-4.translation: Hero of fearsome valour in battle, best of leapers, why do you not speak to me today, helpless and alone?
ramayana-4-20-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-5.translation: Rise, tiger among monkeys, and take the best bed. The best of kings do not lie on the ground like this.
ramayana-4-20-5.meaning: She cannot bear seeing him on the ground.
ramayana-4-20-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-6.translation: Surely the earth is very dear to you, lord of the earth, since even lifeless you embrace her with your limbs and leave me.
ramayana-4-20-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-7.translation: Clearly, hero, by following dharma you have built another lovely city like Kishkindha on the road to heaven.
ramayana-4-20-7.meaning: She imagines him going to heaven.
ramayana-4-20-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-8.translation: The pleasures we shared with you in the honey-scented forests, you have now brought to an end.
ramayana-4-20-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-9.translation: Joyless and hopeless, I am sunk in an ocean of grief now that you, leader of great leaders, have died.
ramayana-4-20-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-10.translation: My heart must be very hard, for seeing you killed on the ground, burning with grief, it does not burst into a thousand pieces today.
ramayana-4-20-10.meaning: She wonders how her heart survives.
ramayana-4-20-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-11.translation: You took Sugriva's wife and banished him. This is the result of that, lord of monkeys.
ramayana-4-20-11.meaning: Tara sees Vali's fate as the fruit of his deeds.
ramayana-4-20-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-12.translation: Out of delusion you rebuked me, though I wished only your good and spoke helpful words, wanting the best for the monkey king.
ramayana-4-20-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-13.translation: Surely it was Time, beyond doubt, that ended your life, by which you were forced helplessly into Sugriva's power.
ramayana-4-20-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-14.translation: Wretched as I am, never having known sorrow before, I will live a pitiful widow's life of grief and pain, like one without a protector.
ramayana-4-20-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-15.translation: Heroic Angada, raised with love, tender and used to comfort, what state will he live in with his uncle mad with anger?
ramayana-4-20-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-16.translation: Son, look well at your father, who loved dharma. It will be hard for you to see him again, my child.
ramayana-4-20-16.meaning: She urges Angada to say goodbye.
ramayana-4-20-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-17.translation: Comfort your son and give him your last message. Kiss him on the head, for you are setting out on a long journey.
ramayana-4-20-17.meaning: She asks Vali to bless Angada.
ramayana-4-20-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-18.translation: Rama has done a great deed in killing you and has freed himself from his debt to Sugriva by keeping his promise.
ramayana-4-20-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-19.translation: Have your wish, Sugriva. You will get Ruma back. Enjoy the kingdom without worry. Your brother, your enemy, is struck down.
ramayana-4-20-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-20.translation: Why do you not speak to me lovingly as I lament like this? Look at these many fine wives of yours, lord of monkeys.
ramayana-4-20-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-21.translation: Hearing her lament, the monkey women all around took hold of the wretched Angada and wailed in sorrow.
ramayana-4-20-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-22.translation: Hero with armlets on your arms, why do you leave Angada and set out on a long journey today? It is not right to leave a son so full of virtue, you who love your son.
ramayana-4-20-22.meaning: Tara asks how he can leave Angada.
ramayana-4-20-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-23.translation: What wrong have I or your son done you, my lord of lovely dress, that you leave your companion today and go to Yama's realm? This is unkind, hero.
ramayana-4-20-23.meaning: She asks what they did to deserve this.
ramayana-4-20-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-24.translation: If I did anything unkind to you without thinking, long-armed lord of the monkey race, forgive me. I bow my head to your feet, hero.
ramayana-4-20-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-20-25.translation: Weeping piteously beside her husband with the monkey women, Tara of faultless beauty resolved to fast to death, sitting on the ground where Vali lay.
ramayana-4-20-25.meaning: Tara resolves to die with Vali.
ramayana-4-20-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 20: Tara laments over the dying Vali.

ramayana-4-21-1.translation: Then Hanuman, leader of monkey troops, gently comforted Tara, who had fallen like a star from the sky.
ramayana-4-21-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-2.translation: Whatever a being does from virtue or fault, it receives calmly after death as the fruit of its own deeds, good or bad.
ramayana-4-21-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-3.translation: You who should be pitied, whom do you pity? Wretched, whom do you feel sorry for? Who should grieve for whom in this body, which is like a bubble?
ramayana-4-21-3.meaning: Life is fleeting like a bubble.
ramayana-4-21-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-4.translation: You, mother of a living son, should look after young Angada. Think of the steps to be taken for his future.
ramayana-4-21-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-5.translation: You know how uncertain the coming and going of beings is. So, wise lady, one should do good that leads beyond this world.
ramayana-4-21-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-6.translation: He on whom thousands, millions and hundreds of millions of monkeys depended for their share has reached his destined end.
ramayana-4-21-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-7.translation: Since he saw his aims by justice and was devoted to conciliation, generosity and forgiveness, he has gone to the world won by dharma. You should not grieve for him.
ramayana-4-21-7.meaning: Vali has gone to a good place.
ramayana-4-21-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-8.translation: All the monkeys, your son Angada, and the kingdom of monkeys and bears now have you as their protector, blameless one.
ramayana-4-21-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-9.translation: Gently guide these two who burn with grief, lady. Supported by you, let Angada rule the earth.
ramayana-4-21-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-10.translation: Let everything be done for the king as tradition holds and as the moment demands. This is the decree of Time.
ramayana-4-21-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-11.translation: Let the monkey king receive his funeral rites and Angada be crowned. Seeing your son on the lion throne, you will find peace.
ramayana-4-21-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-12.translation: Hearing his words, Tara, pained by her husband's death, gave her answer to Hanuman standing there.
ramayana-4-21-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-13.translation: Better than a hundred sons like Angada is to embrace the body of this hero, even dead.
ramayana-4-21-13.meaning: Tara chooses to stay with Vali.
ramayana-4-21-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-14.translation: I have no authority over the monkey kingdom or over Angada. His uncle Sugriva is next in line for all duties.
ramayana-4-21-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-15.translation: This thought should not be held about Angada, Hanuman. A father is a son's guardian, not a mother, best of monkeys.
ramayana-4-21-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-21-16.translation: Nothing here or hereafter is better for me than the shelter of the monkey king. This bed of a hero killed facing the enemy is the one fit for me to share.
ramayana-4-21-16.meaning: Tara wants to join Vali in death.
ramayana-4-21-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 21: Hanuman consoles Tara and urges that Angada be crowned; Tara wishes only to stay by Vali.

ramayana-4-22-1.translation: Vali, his life ebbing and breathing faintly, looked all around and first saw Sugriva in front of his son.
ramayana-4-22-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-2.translation: Speaking clearly and with affection, Vali addressed Sugriva, lord of monkeys, who had won the victory.
ramayana-4-22-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-3.translation: Sugriva, do not take it amiss that I was dragged by force by fate and delusion of mind into wrongdoing.
ramayana-4-22-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-4.translation: I think, dear one, happiness was not meant for us both at the same time. The love that brothers share turned out otherwise for us.
ramayana-4-22-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-5.translation: Take the kingdom of these forest dwellers this very day, and know that I am going today to the realm of Yama.
ramayana-4-22-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-6.translation: I am quickly giving up my life, my kingdom, this great fortune, and my great and spotless fame.
ramayana-4-22-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-7.translation: In this state, hero, I will tell you something. Even if it is hard to do, king, you must do it.
ramayana-4-22-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-8.translation: Look at Angada lying on the ground, his face full of tears, a boy used to comfort and raised in happiness, yet no fool.
ramayana-4-22-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-9.translation: Protect in every way my son, dearer to me than life, as your own son. He lacks me but lacks nothing else.
ramayana-4-22-9.meaning: Care for Angada as your own.
ramayana-4-22-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-10.translation: Be his giver and protector in every way, lord of monkeys, and give him safety in danger as I did.
ramayana-4-22-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-11.translation: This glorious son of Tara, your equal in valour, will be at your front in killing those demons.
ramayana-4-22-11.meaning: Angada will be a great warrior.
ramayana-4-22-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-12.translation: Strong and swift, young Angada, Tara's son, will show his valour in battle and do deeds worthy of him.
ramayana-4-22-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-13.translation: This daughter of Sushena is fully skilled in judging subtle matters and reading omens of every kind.
ramayana-4-22-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-14.translation: Whatever she says is good should be done without doubt. Nothing Tara thinks ever turns out otherwise.
ramayana-4-22-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-15.translation: You must do Raghava's task without hesitation. Not doing it would be wrong, and if dishonoured he might destroy you.
ramayana-4-22-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-16.translation: And put on this heavenly golden garland, Sugriva. Great glory dwells in it, which would leave it when I die.
ramayana-4-22-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-17.translation: Spoken to this way by Vali out of brotherly love, Sugriva lost his joy and became sad again, like the moon seized by an eclipse.
ramayana-4-22-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-18.translation: Calmed by Vali's words, doing what was right and alert, he took the golden garland with permission.
ramayana-4-22-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-19.translation: Having given the golden garland, Vali, ready for the passage after death, saw his son standing there and spoke to Angada with love.
ramayana-4-22-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-20.translation: Respect time and place now, bear the pleasant and the unpleasant, endure joy and sorrow in their season, and be obedient to Sugriva.
ramayana-4-22-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-21.translation: Sugriva will not indulge you as I always did, mighty-armed one, if you behave that way.
ramayana-4-22-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-22.translation: Do not side with his foes or go with his enemies, subduer of enemies. Be devoted to your master's interests, self-controlled and obedient to Sugriva.
ramayana-4-22-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-23.translation: Do not be too familiar, nor too distant. Both are great faults, so keep to the middle.
ramayana-4-22-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-24.translation: Having said this, his eyes rolling and pierced by the arrow, his fearsome teeth bared, he breathed his last.
ramayana-4-22-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-25.translation: When the heroic lord of monkeys was killed, the monkeys found no peace, like cows in a great forest with lions when the bull of the herd is killed.
ramayana-4-22-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-22-26.translation: Then Tara, plunged in an ocean of grief, looked at her dead husband's face, embraced Vali and sank to the ground, like a vine clinging to a great tree cut down.
ramayana-4-22-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 22: the dying Vali reconciles with Sugriva, entrusts Angada to him, gives him Indra's garland, and dies.

ramayana-4-23-1.translation: Then, kissing the monkey king's face, Tara spoke to her husband, now dead and gone from the world.
ramayana-4-23-1.meaning: Tara speaks to Vali one last time.
ramayana-4-23-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-2.translation: You lie in pain on the hard, stony ground, hero, because you did not follow my words.
ramayana-4-23-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-3.translation: Surely the earth is dearer to you than I am, monkey king, for you lie embracing her and do not answer me.
ramayana-4-23-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-4.translation: Now Sugriva is the hero, rash and dear one. The chiefs of bears and monkeys will now serve him as mighty.
ramayana-4-23-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-5.translation: Hearing these painful laments and Angada grieving, and these words of mine, why do you not wake?
ramayana-4-23-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-6.translation: This is the hero's bed on which you lie killed in battle, where you once laid low your enemies.
ramayana-4-23-6.meaning: He lies where his enemies once fell.
ramayana-4-23-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-7.translation: My dear, of pure nature and noble birth, lover of battle, giver of honour, you have gone and left me alone and unprotected.
ramayana-4-23-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-8.translation: A wise man should not give his daughter to a hero. See me, a hero's wife, made a widow in an instant.
ramayana-4-23-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-9.translation: My pride is broken, my lasting refuge is broken, and I am sunk in a vast, bottomless ocean of grief.
ramayana-4-23-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-10.translation: My heart must be made of stone, so hard that it has not broken into a hundred pieces seeing my husband killed.
ramayana-4-23-10.meaning: She marvels that she still lives.
ramayana-4-23-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-11.translation: My friend and husband, dear to me by nature, a hero brave in battle, has met his death.
ramayana-4-23-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-12.translation: A woman without her husband, even if she has sons and is full of wealth and grain, is called a widow by the wise.
ramayana-4-23-12.meaning: Loss of a spouse is a loss nothing can fill.
ramayana-4-23-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-13.translation: You lie, hero, in a circle of blood from your own body, as if on a bed with a crimson cover.
ramayana-4-23-13.meaning: Vali lies in his own blood.
ramayana-4-23-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-14.translation: Your body is covered all over with dust and blood, and I cannot embrace you with my arms, bull among monkeys.
ramayana-4-23-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-15.translation: Today Sugriva has achieved his aim in this terrible feud, his fear taken away by one arrow loosed by Rama.
ramayana-4-23-15.meaning: Sugriva is now free of fear.
ramayana-4-23-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-16.translation: The arrow lodged in your heart stops me from touching your body as I look at you, now that you are dead.
ramayana-4-23-16.meaning: The arrow keeps her from him.
ramayana-4-23-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-17.translation: Then Nila drew out the arrow from his body, like a blazing venomous snake hidden in a mountain cave.
ramayana-4-23-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-18.translation: As the arrow was drawn out, its brilliance shone like the sun's ray caught on the peak of the setting mountain.
ramayana-4-23-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-19.translation: Streams of blood fell from his wounds everywhere, like streams from a mountain mixed with red ochre.
ramayana-4-23-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-20.translation: Wiping her husband covered with battle dust, she bathed the hero struck by the weapon with tears from her eyes.
ramayana-4-23-20.meaning: Tara washes him with her tears.
ramayana-4-23-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-21.translation: Seeing her husband killed, all his limbs soaked with blood, Tara said to her tawny-eyed son Angada:
ramayana-4-23-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-22.translation: See your father's last, terrible state, son. The long feud has ended through his wrong deeds.
ramayana-4-23-22.meaning: The feud has ended in death.
ramayana-4-23-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-23.translation: Bow to the king, your father, giver of honour, bright as the rising sun, who is going to the abode of Yama.
ramayana-4-23-23.meaning: She asks Angada to pay respects.
ramayana-4-23-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-24.translation: Told this, Angada rose and took his father's feet in his strong round arms, saying: I am Angada.
ramayana-4-23-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-25.translation: Why do you not say to Angada as he bows, as before: Live long, son?
ramayana-4-23-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-26.translation: With my son I sit beside you who are lifeless, like a cow with her calf beside a bull just killed by a lion.
ramayana-4-23-26.meaning: Tara and Angada sit by Vali.
ramayana-4-23-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-27.translation: Having performed the sacrifice of battle with the waters of many weapons, how could you bathe in this final bath without me, your wife?
ramayana-4-23-27.meaning: She compares his death to a rite done without her.
ramayana-4-23-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-28.translation: Why do I not see here the gold garland that the king of gods gave you, pleased with you in battle?
ramayana-4-23-28.meaning: His garland has gone to Sugriva.
ramayana-4-23-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-29.translation: Royal glory does not leave you even in death, giver of honour, as light stays on the king of mountains when the sun turns away.
ramayana-4-23-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-23-30.translation: You did not heed my wholesome words, and I could not stop you. With you killed in battle, I and my son are destroyed, and fortune leaves me here along with you.
ramayana-4-23-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 23: Tara mourns Vali's death, and the arrow is drawn from his body.

ramayana-4-24-1.translation: Seeing Vali dead, Raghava, scorcher of enemies, then spoke courteous words to Sugriva.
ramayana-4-24-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-2.translation: The dead are not helped by grief and lament. You should attend to what must be done next.
ramayana-4-24-2.meaning: Grief does not help the dead.
ramayana-4-24-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-3.translation: Worldly custom must be followed, and you have shed your tears. No act can be done beyond its proper time.
ramayana-4-24-3.meaning: Act when the time is right.
ramayana-4-24-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-4.translation: Destiny is the fixed cause in the world, destiny the means of action, destiny the cause of all beings' engagements here.
ramayana-4-24-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-5.translation: No one is the doer of anything, nor master over his assignment. The world moves by its nature, and Time is its final support.
ramayana-4-24-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-6.translation: Time does not pass beyond Time, nor does Time fail. Having reached its nature, nothing goes beyond it.
ramayana-4-24-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-7.translation: Time has no kinship, no cause, no favouritism for valour, no ties of friend or relative, and it is not under anyone's control.
ramayana-4-24-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-8.translation: But one who sees well must look at the workings of Time. Dharma, wealth and pleasure are all arranged in the order of Time.
ramayana-4-24-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-9.translation: From here Vali has gone to his own nature and received the fruit of his deeds, purified by the union of dharma, wealth and desire, lord of monkeys.
ramayana-4-24-9.meaning: Vali has gone to his reward.
ramayana-4-24-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-10.translation: Through fulfilling his own duty, the great one has won heaven, not clinging to his life.
ramayana-4-24-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-11.translation: This is the best destiny, which the leader of monkey troops has reached. So enough of grieving; let what is timely be done.
ramayana-4-24-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-12.translation: When Rama finished speaking, Lakshmana, slayer of enemy heroes, spoke courteously to Sugriva, who was dazed.
ramayana-4-24-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-13.translation: Sugriva, perform his funeral rites now, together with Tara and Angada, for the cremation of Vali.
ramayana-4-24-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-14.translation: Order plenty of dry wood and heavenly sandalwood for Vali's last rites.
ramayana-4-24-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time and asks them to perform the funeral rites.

ramayana-4-24-15.translation: Comfort Angada, who is downcast. Do not be foolish, for this city now depends on you.
ramayana-4-24-15.meaning: Lakshmana reminds Sugriva of his duty.
ramayana-4-24-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-16.translation: Let Angada bring garlands, clothes of many kinds, ghee, oil, perfumes and whatever else is needed next.
ramayana-4-24-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-17.translation: Tara, quickly bring a palanquin and come. Speed is a virtue, especially at a time like this.
ramayana-4-24-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-18.translation: Let monkeys fit to carry a palanquin get ready. Strong and capable, they will carry Vali out.
ramayana-4-24-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-19.translation: Having said this to Sugriva, Lakshmana, joy of Sumitra and slayer of enemy heroes, stood beside his brother.
ramayana-4-24-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-20.translation: Hearing Lakshmana's words, Tara, flustered, quickly entered the cave, his mind set on the palanquin.
ramayana-4-24-20.meaning: The monkey Tara fetches the bier.
ramayana-4-24-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-21.translation: Bringing the palanquin, Tara set it down, carried by heroic monkeys fit for the task.
ramayana-4-24-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-22.translation: Then Sugriva lifted Vali and, crying out, placed him on the palanquin together with Angada.
ramayana-4-24-22.meaning: Sugriva places Vali on the bier.
ramayana-4-24-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-23.translation: Having placed the lifeless Vali on the palanquin, adorned with many ornaments, garlands and clothes,
ramayana-4-24-23.meaning: Vali is adorned for the last time.
ramayana-4-24-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-24.translation: King Sugriva, lord of monkeys, then ordered: Let my noble brother's funeral be performed fittingly.
ramayana-4-24-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-25.translation: Let monkeys go in front scattering many kinds of jewels, and the palanquin follow behind.
ramayana-4-24-25.meaning: Jewels are scattered before the bier.
ramayana-4-24-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-26.translation: As the special splendours of kings are seen on earth, so they quickly performed Vali's funeral.
ramayana-4-24-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-27.translation: Quickly taking Angada with them, the monkey Tara and all the others went, wailing, their kinsman killed.
ramayana-4-24-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-28.translation: Tara and all the monkey women, their leader killed, followed their husband, wailing in piteous voices.
ramayana-4-24-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-29.translation: With the sound of the monkey women weeping in the forest, all the woods and hills seemed to wail on every side.
ramayana-4-24-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-30.translation: On a secluded sandbank of a mountain river surrounded by water, many forest monkeys built a pyre.
ramayana-4-24-30.meaning: They build the pyre by a river.
ramayana-4-24-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-31.translation: The bearers lowered the palanquin from their shoulders and all stood apart, full of grief.
ramayana-4-24-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-32.translation: Then Tara, seeing her husband lying on the palanquin, took his head on her lap and lamented in deep sorrow.
ramayana-4-24-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-33.translation: Why do you look at these people stricken with grief? Even in death, giver of honour, your face seems joyful and has the colour of the setting sun, as if alive.
ramayana-4-24-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-34.translation: Time in the form of Rama drags you away, monkey, Time by whom we all were made widows with one arrow in battle.
ramayana-4-24-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-35.translation: These are your monkey queens, always dear to you, king of kings, come this long way on foot. Why do you not wake?
ramayana-4-24-35.meaning: She calls on him to wake.
ramayana-4-24-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-36.translation: Are these not your beloved wives with faces like the moon? Why do you not now look at Sugriva, lord of monkeys?
ramayana-4-24-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-37.translation: These ministers of yours, king, Tara and the others, and these townspeople sit around you, sinless one.
ramayana-4-24-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-38.translation: Dismiss them as is proper, subduer of foes, and then we will all play in the forests, merry with wine.
ramayana-4-24-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-39.translation: As Tara lamented this way, flooded with grief for her husband, the monkey women, themselves worn by sorrow, raised her up.
ramayana-4-24-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-40.translation: Then Angada, weeping, his senses stunned by grief, placed his father on the pyre with Sugriva.
ramayana-4-24-40.meaning: Angada places Vali on the pyre.
ramayana-4-24-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-41.translation: Then, lighting the fire as the rites require, he walked around it keeping it to his left, distraught at his father setting out on the long road.
ramayana-4-24-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-42.translation: Having cremated Vali properly, the monkeys came to the lovely cool river to make water offerings.
ramayana-4-24-42.meaning: They offer water for the dead.
ramayana-4-24-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-43.translation: Gathered there, putting Angada in front, with Sugriva and Tara, they poured water for Vali.
ramayana-4-24-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-24-44.translation: Mighty Kakutstha, saddened as Sugriva was sad and sharing his grief, had the funeral rites carried out.
ramayana-4-24-44.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 24: Rama tells the mourners that all beings are governed by Time, and Vali is cremated with royal honours.

ramayana-4-25-1.translation: Then the monkey chiefs surrounded and attended Sugriva, burning with grief, his clothes still wet.
ramayana-4-25-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-2.translation: Approaching mighty-armed Rama, tireless in action, they all stood with folded hands like sages before Brahma.
ramayana-4-25-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-3.translation: Then Hanuman, son of the Wind, like a golden mountain, his face like the rising sun, spoke with folded hands:
ramayana-4-25-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-4.translation: By your grace, lord, Sugriva has won this great ancestral kingdom of the monkeys, so hard to gain.
ramayana-4-25-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-5.translation: With your permission he will enter the fine city and arrange all affairs with his friends.
ramayana-4-25-5.meaning: Sugriva asks leave to enter the city.
ramayana-4-25-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-6.translation: After bathing in the rites with many perfumes and herbs, he will honour you especially with jewels and garlands.
ramayana-4-25-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-7.translation: Please come to this lovely mountain cave and become our lord, delighting the monkeys.
ramayana-4-25-7.meaning: Hanuman invites Rama to the city.
ramayana-4-25-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-8.translation: Told this by Hanuman, Raghava, slayer of enemy heroes, wise and skilled in speech, replied to Hanuman:
ramayana-4-25-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-9.translation: For fourteen years, gentle Hanuman, I will not enter a village or a city, keeping my father's command.
ramayana-4-25-9.meaning: Rama keeps his vow of exile.
ramayana-4-25-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-10.translation: Let heroic Sugriva, bull among monkeys, enter the rich and lovely cave properly and quickly be crowned king.
ramayana-4-25-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-11.translation: Having said this to Hanuman, Rama said to Sugriva: Crown this hero Angada as crown prince too.
ramayana-4-25-11.meaning: Rama asks that Angada be heir.
ramayana-4-25-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-12.translation: This is the first month of the rains, Shravana, when the waters come. The four months called the rainy season have begun, gentle one.
ramayana-4-25-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-13.translation: This is not the time for a campaign. Enter your fine city. I will live on this mountain with Lakshmana, gentle one.
ramayana-4-25-13.meaning: They will wait out the rains.
ramayana-4-25-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-14.translation: This mountain cave is lovely and spacious, airy, with plenty of water and plenty of lotuses and lilies, gentle one.
ramayana-4-25-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.
