ramayana-4-25-15.translation: When the month of Kartika comes, strive for Ravana's killing. This is our agreement, gentle one. Enter your home, be crowned king, and gladden your friends.
ramayana-4-25-15.meaning: They agree to begin after the rains.
ramayana-4-25-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-16.translation: Given leave by Rama, Sugriva, bull among monkeys, entered lovely Kishkindha, once ruled by Vali.
ramayana-4-25-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-17.translation: Thousands of monkeys greeted the lord of monkeys joyfully as he entered and surrounded him on all sides.
ramayana-4-25-17.meaning: The monkeys welcome their new king.
ramayana-4-25-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-18.translation: Then all the subjects, seeing the lord of the monkey hosts, bowed with their heads to the ground, attentive.
ramayana-4-25-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-19.translation: Mighty Sugriva spoke with all the subjects, raised them up, and entered his brother's pleasant inner apartments.
ramayana-4-25-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-20.translation: When Sugriva came out again, his friends consecrated the bull among monkeys as the immortals consecrated thousand-eyed Indra.
ramayana-4-25-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-21.translation: They brought him a white umbrella adorned with gold and two white yak-tail fans with golden handles, bringing glory.
ramayana-4-25-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-22.translation: Likewise all kinds of jewels, all seeds and herbs, shoots and flowers of milky trees,
ramayana-4-25-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-23.translation: white clothes, white unguent, fragrant garlands of land and water flowers,
ramayana-4-25-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-24.translation: heavenly sandalwood and many kinds of perfumes, unbroken rice, gold, priyangu, honey and ghee,
ramayana-4-25-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-25.translation: curd, a tiger skin and boar-skin sandals. Taking unguents, yellow pigment and red arsenic, sixteen fine maidens came there joyfully.
ramayana-4-25-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-26.translation: Then, at the proper time and by the rites, having pleased the best of brahmins with jewels, clothes and food for the best of monkeys,
ramayana-4-25-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-27.translation: those who knew the mantras offered oblations purified by mantras into the blazing fire spread with kusha grass.
ramayana-4-25-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-28.translation: Then on a lovely palace terrace adorned with colourful garlands, on a golden base covered with fine rugs,
ramayana-4-25-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-29.translation: they seated him facing east on the best seat with many mantras. Gathering water from rivers and streams and from sacred places all around,
ramayana-4-25-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-30.translation: and bringing it from all the seas, the bull-like monkeys placed the pure, clean water in golden jars.
ramayana-4-25-30.meaning: Water from every sea is gathered.
ramayana-4-25-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-31.translation: With fine bull horns and golden pitchers, by the rite seen in the scriptures and ordained by the great sages,
ramayana-4-25-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-32.translation: Gaja, Gavaksha, Gavaya, Sharabha, Gandhamadana, Mainda, Dvivida, Hanuman, Jambavan and Nala
ramayana-4-25-32.meaning: The great monkey leaders take part.
ramayana-4-25-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-33.translation: consecrated Sugriva with clear, fragrant water, as the Vasus consecrated thousand-eyed Indra.
ramayana-4-25-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-34.translation: When Sugriva was consecrated, all the great monkey chiefs shouted for joy there in their thousands.
ramayana-4-25-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-35.translation: Following Rama's word, Sugriva, chief of monkeys, embraced Angada and made him crown prince.
ramayana-4-25-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-36.translation: When Angada was consecrated, the kind-hearted monkeys honoured Sugriva, saying: Well done, well done!
ramayana-4-25-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-37.translation: Lovely Kishkindha in its mountain cave became full of happy, well-fed people and bright with banners and flags.
ramayana-4-25-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-25-38.translation: Having reported the great coronation to great Rama, the mighty leader of the monkey host, having got back his wife Ruma, gained the kingdom as Indra did heaven.
ramayana-4-25-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 25: Sugriva is crowned king of Kishkindha and Angada is made crown prince; Rama waits out the rains.

ramayana-4-26-1.translation: When Sugriva was crowned and had entered the cave, Rama came with his brother to Mount Prasravana.
ramayana-4-26-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-2.translation: It echoed with tigers and deer, was full of lions with fearsome roars, hidden by many bushes and creepers and crowded with trees.
ramayana-4-26-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-3.translation: Home to bears, monkeys, langurs and wildcats, the mountain was like a mass of clouds and always had pure water.
ramayana-4-26-3.meaning: The mountain is full of life.
ramayana-4-26-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-4.translation: On the peak of that mountain Rama and Lakshmana took a large, long cave as their dwelling.
ramayana-4-26-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-5.translation: Righteous Raghava lived there with Lakshmana on Mount Prasravana with its many lovely valleys and groves.
ramayana-4-26-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-6.translation: Though that mountain was very pleasant and rich in resources, Rama found no joy at all living there, remembering his wife who had been taken, dearer to him than life.
ramayana-4-26-6.meaning: Rama cannot be happy without Sita.
ramayana-4-26-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-7.translation: Especially when he saw the moon rising over the eastern hill, sleep would not come to him when he went to bed at night.
ramayana-4-26-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-8.translation: Seeing Kakutstha grieving always, his mind clouded with tears from that sorrow, his brother Lakshmana, sharing his pain, spoke consoling words:
ramayana-4-26-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-9.translation: Enough of this anguish, hero. You should not grieve. Everything fails for one who grieves, as you know.
ramayana-4-26-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-10.translation: You are devoted to action in the world, devoted to the gods, a believer, righteous and resolute, Raghava.
ramayana-4-26-10.meaning: Lakshmana reminds Rama who he is.
ramayana-4-26-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-11.translation: Without resolve you cannot kill your enemy in battle, especially that crooked demon, even with all your valour.
ramayana-4-26-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-12.translation: Uproot your grief and make your resolve firm. Then destroy that demon with all his followers.
ramayana-4-26-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-13.translation: Kakutstha, you could overturn even the earth with its seas, forests and mountains. How much more Ravana!
ramayana-4-26-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-14.translation: I am only awakening your sleeping strength, like a fire hidden under ashes roused in time with bright offerings.
ramayana-4-26-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-15.translation: Honouring Lakshmana's good and helpful words, Raghava spoke these words to his loving friend:
ramayana-4-26-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-16.translation: You have said, Lakshmana, what should be said by one who is devoted, loving, well-meaning and truly brave.
ramayana-4-26-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-17.translation: I have given up this grief that ruins all tasks. I will rouse my strength, unchecked in valour.
ramayana-4-26-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-18.translation: I await the autumn, now that the rainy season has come. Then I will kill that demon with his kingdom and followers.
ramayana-4-26-18.meaning: Rama will act after the rains.
ramayana-4-26-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-19.translation: Hearing Rama's words, Lakshmana, delighting his friends, was glad and spoke again:
ramayana-4-26-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-20.translation: These words are worthy of you, destroyer of enemies. Now, Kakutstha, you have returned to your true nature.
ramayana-4-26-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-21.translation: Knowing your own strength, you should make it real. What you have said fits your learning and your lineage.
ramayana-4-26-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-22.translation: So, tiger among men, thinking of how to defeat the enemy, let the rainy season that has come pass, Raghava.
ramayana-4-26-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-26-23.translation: Hold back your anger and wait for autumn. Bear these four months with me, living on this mountain where lions roam, building up your strength, ready to kill the enemy.
ramayana-4-26-23.meaning: Patience now will bring victory later.
ramayana-4-26-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 26: Rama and Lakshmana live on Mount Prasravana during the rains; Lakshmana lifts Rama out of his grief.

ramayana-4-27-1.translation: Having killed Vali and crowned Sugriva, Rama, living on the ridge of Malyavan, said to Lakshmana:
ramayana-4-27-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-2.translation: The season of rain has come. Look at the sky covered with clouds like mountains.
ramayana-4-27-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-3.translation: Having drunk the essence of the seas through the sun's rays and carried it like a child for nine months, the sky now gives birth to the elixir of rain.
ramayana-4-27-3.meaning: Rain is the sky's long-awaited gift.
ramayana-4-27-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-4.translation: One could climb into the sky on the stairways of clouds and adorn the sun with garlands of kutaja and arjuna flowers.
ramayana-4-27-4.meaning: The clouds look like steps to the sky.
ramayana-4-27-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-5.translation: With copper-red clouds risen from the glow of dusk, paler at the edges, the sky looks as if its wounds were bound with soft bandages of cloud.
ramayana-4-27-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-6.translation: With gentle breezes for its sighs, tinted with the sandal of twilight and pale clouds, the sky seems sick with love.
ramayana-4-27-6.meaning: The sky seems to long like a lover.
ramayana-4-27-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-7.translation: This earth, worn by the heat and now flooded with new rain, sheds tears like Sita burning with grief.
ramayana-4-27-7.meaning: The steaming earth reminds Rama of Sita's tears.
ramayana-4-27-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-8.translation: The winds released from the clouds' bellies, cool as kahlara lilies and scented with ketaki, could almost be drunk from cupped hands.
ramayana-4-27-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-9.translation: This mountain with flowering arjuna trees, scented with ketaki, is bathed by the rain like Sugriva consecrated when his enemy was quelled.
ramayana-4-27-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-10.translation: Wearing clouds like black deerskins and streams of rain like sacred threads, their caves filled with wind, the mountains seem like students reciting the Veda.
ramayana-4-27-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-11.translation: Struck by lightning as if by golden whips, with thunder rumbling within, the sky seems to cry out in pain.
ramayana-4-27-11.meaning: Thunder sounds like a cry of pain.
ramayana-4-27-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-12.translation: The lightning flashing against the dark cloud seems to me like poor Vaidehi struggling in Ravana's lap.
ramayana-4-27-12.meaning: Lightning reminds Rama of Sita's struggle.
ramayana-4-27-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-13.translation: These directions, so pleasing to lovers, are now blotted out, as if smeared with clouds, the planets and moon hidden.
ramayana-4-27-13.meaning: Clouds hide the stars and moon.
ramayana-4-27-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-14.translation: See, Lakshmana, the kutaja trees blooming on the mountain slopes, here and there choked with mist and eager for the rains, kindling longing in me, overcome by grief.
ramayana-4-27-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-15.translation: The dust has settled, the wind is cool today, the troubles of summer heat have ceased. Kings have halted their campaigns, and travellers go home.
ramayana-4-27-15.meaning: The rains bring everything to rest.
ramayana-4-27-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-16.translation: The chakravaka birds, eager to live by Lake Manasa, have set out with their mates. On roads broken by constant rain, vehicles do not move.
ramayana-4-27-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-17.translation: The sky, strewn with clouds, shines bright in some places and dark in others, here and there blocked by mountains, like the face of a calm great ocean.
ramayana-4-27-17.meaning: The sky looks like a calm sea.
ramayana-4-27-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-18.translation: Mountain streams rush faster, carrying new water reddened by mountain minerals and mixed with sarja and kadamba flowers, followed by the cries of peacocks.
ramayana-4-27-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-19.translation: Juicy rose-apples, dark as bees, are eaten freely, and ripe mangoes of many colours, shaken by the wind, fall to the ground.
ramayana-4-27-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-20.translation: With lightning for banners and garlands of cranes, shaped like the peaks of great mountains, the clouds roar loudly like mad elephants in battle.
ramayana-4-27-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-21.translation: The line of cranes, longing for the clouds and flying joyfully, looks like a garland of fine white lotuses swaying in the wind, hung on the sky.
ramayana-4-27-21.meaning: Flying cranes look like a garland.
ramayana-4-27-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-22.translation: Sleep slowly comes to Keshava, the river quickly reaches the sea, the happy crane goes to the cloud, and the loving woman goes to her beloved.
ramayana-4-27-22.meaning: All things seek their union in the rains.
ramayana-4-27-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-23.translation: The forests are alive with dancing peacocks, the kadambas are in bloom, the bulls share desire with the cows, and the earth is lovely with crops and woods.
ramayana-4-27-23.meaning: The land is full of life.
ramayana-4-27-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-24.translation: The rivers flow, the clouds rain, the mad elephants trumpet, the forests shine, separated lovers brood, peacocks dance and monkeys take comfort.
ramayana-4-27-24.meaning: Each creature responds to the rains.
ramayana-4-27-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-25.translation: Delighted by the scent of ketaki flowers, great elephants by the forest falls, deafened by the sound of the cascades, trumpet with the peacocks in their passion.
ramayana-4-27-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-26.translation: Beaten by the falling rain, hanging on kadamba branches, the bees slowly lose the intoxication they had just drawn deep from the flowers' nectar.
ramayana-4-27-26.meaning: Rain washes the bees from the flowers.
ramayana-4-27-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-27.translation: The branches of the rose-apple trees, laden with ripe juicy fruit like heaps of charcoal, look as if covered with swarms of bees.
ramayana-4-27-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-28.translation: The clouds, adorned with lightning banners and roaring deep and loud, look like elephants ready for battle.
ramayana-4-27-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-29.translation: A mad elephant following the path through the mountain forests, hearing the thunder and thinking it a rival, eager to fight, turns back.
ramayana-4-27-29.meaning: An elephant mistakes thunder for a rival.
ramayana-4-27-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-30.translation: Thirsty birds with ruffled feathers joyfully drink the pearl-like rainwater caught in cups of leaves, a gift from the king of gods.
ramayana-4-27-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-31.translation: Dark clouds full of new rain cling to dark clouds and shine like burnt mountains rooted against burnt mountains.
ramayana-4-27-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-32.translation: Great elephants are in rut, bulls are happy, lions rest in the forests, the great mountains are lovely and quiet, and Indra plays with the clouds.
ramayana-4-27-32.meaning: Everything is at rest or at play.
ramayana-4-27-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-33.translation: The kings' campaigns are over and their armies turn back. The rains have made enmities and roads alike impassable.
ramayana-4-27-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-34.translation: In the month of Praushthapada, the season for study has come for brahmins wishing to recite the Veda and for the Sama singers.
ramayana-4-27-34.meaning: The rains are the season for study.
ramayana-4-27-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-35.translation: Surely Bharata, lord of the treasury, having finished his work and gathered his stores, has begun the Ashadhi observance.
ramayana-4-27-35.meaning: Rama thinks of Bharata at home.
ramayana-4-27-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-36.translation: Surely the swelling Sarayu is rising in flood, its roar like Ayodhya's on seeing me come home.
ramayana-4-27-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-37.translation: Sugriva enjoys these rich rains in comfort, his enemy conquered, with his wife, settled in a great kingdom.
ramayana-4-27-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-38.translation: But I, my wife taken and fallen from a great kingdom, sink like a soaked riverbank, Lakshmana.
ramayana-4-27-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-39.translation: My grief is vast, the rains make travel very hard, and Ravana is a great enemy. It all seems endless to me.
ramayana-4-27-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-40.translation: Seeing that this is no time to march and that the roads are very hard, I said nothing to Sugriva, though he bowed to me.
ramayana-4-27-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-41.translation: He has suffered greatly and is reunited with his wife after long. Though my own task weighs heavy, I do not wish to press the monkey.
ramayana-4-27-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-42.translation: Having rested and knowing that the time has come, Sugriva will himself remember the help he received. There is no doubt of that.
ramayana-4-27-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-43.translation: So I wait for the right time, auspicious one, waiting for Sugriva's goodwill and for the rivers to clear.
ramayana-4-27-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-44.translation: A hero who is helped is bound to help in return. One who is ungrateful and does not repay wounds the hearts of the noble.
ramayana-4-27-44.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-45.translation: Told this, Lakshmana, with folded hands, reflected, honoured what was said, and spoke to Rama of lovely appearance, showing his own good insight.
ramayana-4-27-45.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-27-46.translation: Lord of men, the monkey king will soon do all you wish, as you have said. Waiting for autumn, bear this rainy season, firm in your resolve to subdue the enemy.
ramayana-4-27-46.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 27: Rama describes the rainy season to Lakshmana, a celebrated nature passage, while longing for Sita.

ramayana-4-28-1.translation: Seeing the clear sky free of lightning and clouds, ringing with the calls of cranes and bathed in lovely moonlight,
ramayana-4-28-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-2.translation: and Sugriva, his wealth secure but careless in gathering dharma and wealth, given far to the ways of the unworthy, his mind set on private pleasure,
ramayana-4-28-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-3.translation: his work done, his aims achieved, always enjoying the company of women, having gained all the desires he wished for,
ramayana-4-28-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-4.translation: sporting day and night with his beloved wife and with Tara whom he also desired, satisfied and free of anxiety,
ramayana-4-28-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-5.translation: playing like the lord of gods in Nandana with troops of apsaras, leaving affairs to his ministers and not overseeing them,
ramayana-4-28-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-6.translation: the business of the kingdom neglected, living by desire, Hanuman, who was sure of the facts, knew the truth of things and the special duties of the season,
ramayana-4-28-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-7.translation: the son of the Wind, skilled in speech, pleased the monkey king, who knew the truth of words, with sweet, reasoned and charming words.
ramayana-4-28-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-8.translation: Going to the monkey king, Hanuman spoke words that were beneficial, true and wholesome, full of conciliation, dharma, profit and policy, joined with affection and resolved in trust.
ramayana-4-28-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-9.translation: You have gained the kingdom and fame, and your family's fortune has grown. What remains is to secure your friends, and you should do it.
ramayana-4-28-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-10.translation: Whoever always behaves well toward friends and knows the right time, his kingdom, fame and power grow.
ramayana-4-28-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-11.translation: The king whose treasury, army, friends and self all work together enjoys a great kingdom, lord of the earth.
ramayana-4-28-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-12.translation: So you, rich in good conduct and standing on the safe path, should do properly what your friend needs.
ramayana-4-28-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-13.translation: But one who attends to a friend's affairs after the time has passed gains no credit with that friend, even if he does great things.
ramayana-4-28-13.meaning: Late help is not true help.
ramayana-4-28-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-14.translation: Let the search for Vaidehi be made for Raghava. This task of yours, hero, is already past its time, subduer of enemies.
ramayana-4-28-14.meaning: The time to act is now.
ramayana-4-28-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-15.translation: Though he knows the time and is in a hurry, the wise Rama does not tell you the time has passed, king, for he defers to your will.
ramayana-4-28-15.meaning: Rama is too gracious to remind him.
ramayana-4-28-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-16.translation: Raghava is the banner of a flourishing family, a lasting friend, of immeasurable power and himself without equal in virtues.
ramayana-4-28-16.meaning: Rama is a friend worth honouring.
ramayana-4-28-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-17.translation: Do his work, since he did yours first. Lord of monkeys, you should command the best monkeys.
ramayana-4-28-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-18.translation: The time is not yet lost if you act without being urged. But if the task must be urged, the time will have passed.
ramayana-4-28-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-19.translation: You would help even someone who had never helped you, lord of monkeys. How much more him who gave you the kingdom and wealth!
ramayana-4-28-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-20.translation: You are able and brave, lord of the monkey and bear hosts. Why do you hesitate to command what will please the son of Dasharatha?
ramayana-4-28-20.meaning: Sugriva has the power to act.
ramayana-4-28-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-21.translation: Dasharatha's son could bring gods, demons and great serpents under his control with his arrows, but he waits for you to keep your promise.
ramayana-4-28-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-22.translation: Without hesitating to risk his life, he did what you wanted. Let us search for Vaidehi on earth and in the sky.
ramayana-4-28-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-23.translation: Neither gods, gandharvas, asuras, maruts nor yakshas can make him afraid, let alone rakshasas.
ramayana-4-28-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-24.translation: So you should do everything to please Rama, who is so powerful and who first did you a kindness, tawny lord.
ramayana-4-28-24.meaning: Do all you can for Rama.
ramayana-4-28-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-25.translation: Under your command, lord of monkeys, none of us is held back from going below the earth, into the waters, or up into the sky.
ramayana-4-28-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-26.translation: So command who should go where and what each should do for you. You have more than ten million unassailable monkeys, sinless one.
ramayana-4-28-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-27.translation: Hearing his words, well spoken at the right time, Sugriva, strong in character, made a fine decision.
ramayana-4-28-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-28.translation: He ordered Nila, ever active, whom he valued, to gather all the troops from every direction.
ramayana-4-28-28.meaning: Nila is told to muster the army.
ramayana-4-28-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-29.translation: Make sure my whole army and all the troop leaders come together without delay, with the vanguards.
ramayana-4-28-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-30.translation: Let the swift and resolute monkeys guarding the borders quickly bring in the troops at my command, and you yourself then inspect the army.
ramayana-4-28-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-31.translation: Any monkey who does not arrive here within fifteen nights shall be put to death. There is no need for discussion.
ramayana-4-28-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-28-32.translation: With Angada, go to the elder monkeys under my firm command. Having made these arrangements, the mighty lord of monkey chiefs entered his palace.
ramayana-4-28-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 28: when autumn comes, Hanuman reminds Sugriva, lost in pleasure, of his promise to Rama, and Sugriva orders the army to gather.

ramayana-4-29-1.translation: When Sugriva had gone into the cave and the sky was free of clouds, Rama, having spent the rainy season there, was tormented by longing and grief.
ramayana-4-29-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-2.translation: Seeing the pale sky and the clear disc of the moon, and seeing the autumn night bathed in moonlight,
ramayana-4-29-2.meaning: The clear sky reminds him of Sita.
ramayana-4-29-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-3.translation: and realising that Sugriva was living for pleasure, that Janaka's daughter was lost and the time had passed, he fainted in great distress.
ramayana-4-29-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-4.translation: Regaining consciousness after a moment, wise Raghava thought again of Vaidehi, who lived in his heart.
ramayana-4-29-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-5.translation: Sitting on the mountain top adorned with golden minerals, seeing the autumn sky, he went in his mind to his beloved.
ramayana-4-29-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-6.translation: Seeing the clear sky without lightning or clouds, ringing with the calls of cranes, he lamented in a pained voice:
ramayana-4-29-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-7.translation: She who once delighted in the hermitage with the cries of cranes, herself speaking like a crane, how does that young girl find delight now?
ramayana-4-29-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-8.translation: Seeing the flowering asana trees bright as pure gold, how can that young girl be happy, looking for me and not seeing me?
ramayana-4-29-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-9.translation: She who used to wake to the voices of the kalahamsa geese, sweet-voiced and lovely in every limb, how does she wake now?
ramayana-4-29-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-10.translation: Hearing the calls of chakravakas wandering with their mates, how will the lotus-eyed one be?
ramayana-4-29-10.meaning: Pairs of birds will remind her of him.
ramayana-4-29-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-11.translation: Wandering among lakes, rivers, ponds, woods and forests without that fawn-eyed one, I find no happiness today.
ramayana-4-29-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and grows angry at Sugriva's delay.

ramayana-4-29-12.translation: Surely longing, heightened by the beauty of autumn, will torment that lovely one, delicate as she is and parted from me.
ramayana-4-29-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-13.translation: So the prince, best of men, lamented, like the saranga bird crying to Indra for water.
ramayana-4-29-13.meaning: Rama longs like a thirsty bird.
ramayana-4-29-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

keywords.meaning: a bird that drinks only rain

ramayana-4-29-14.translation: Then glorious Lakshmana, who had been wandering the lovely mountain slopes looking for fruit, returned and saw his elder brother.
ramayana-4-29-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-15.translation: Seeing him alone in that lonely place, overcome by unbearable worry and senseless, high-minded Lakshmana, saddened by his brother's grief, spoke to Rama.
ramayana-4-29-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-16.translation: Noble brother, what good is giving in to longing and defeating your own manliness? Your composure is always being stolen away. What use is giving up your discipline?
ramayana-4-29-16.meaning: Lakshmana urges Rama to keep his focus.
ramayana-4-29-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-17.translation: Take up action, calm your mind, use your time in steady focus, rely on your allies' strength, and with an undaunted spirit make your own effort the cause of success.
ramayana-4-29-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-18.translation: Lord of the human race, with you as her protector Janaki cannot easily be held by another. No one, best of heroes, touches a blazing flame and is not burned.
ramayana-4-29-18.meaning: Ravana will pay for taking her.
ramayana-4-29-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-19.translation: Rama spoke to Lakshmana, auspicious and unassailable, words from his own nature, beneficial, wholesome, full of policy, conciliation, dharma and purpose.
ramayana-4-29-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-20.translation: Without doubt the task must be looked to and the right action followed. One should not brood over the fruit of a hard task already begun.
ramayana-4-29-20.meaning: Do the work; do not fret over results.
ramayana-4-29-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-21.translation: Then, thinking of lotus-eyed Maithili, Rama spoke to Lakshmana with a drying face:
ramayana-4-29-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-22.translation: Thousand-eyed Indra, having satisfied the earth with water and ripened the crops, has finished his work and rests.
ramayana-4-29-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-23.translation: The clouds with their deep, soft rumble, which went ahead of mountains and trees, have released their water and are tired, prince.
ramayana-4-29-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-24.translation: The clouds, dark as blue lily petals, having darkened the ten directions, are now calm like elephants whose rut is over.
ramayana-4-29-24.meaning: Calm has returned to the sky.
ramayana-4-29-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-25.translation: The rain winds, heavy with water and swift, scented with kutaja and arjuna, have blown and now ceased, gentle one.
ramayana-4-29-25.meaning: The stormy winds have died down.
ramayana-4-29-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-26.translation: The sound of clouds, elephants, peacocks and waterfalls has suddenly fallen silent, Lakshmana.
ramayana-4-29-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-27.translation: Washed by the great clouds, the mountains with their colourful slopes are clean and shine as if smeared with moonbeams.
ramayana-4-29-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-28.translation: The autumn rivers slowly reveal their sandbanks, like shy young brides.
ramayana-4-29-28.meaning: The rivers shrink and reveal their banks.
ramayana-4-29-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-29.translation: The lakes with clear water shine, gentle one, ringing with ospreys and crowded with flocks of chakravakas.
ramayana-4-29-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-30.translation: The season for campaigns has come for kings bent on conquest and bound in mutual enmity, prince.
ramayana-4-29-30.meaning: It is now time to march.
ramayana-4-29-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-31.translation: This is the first season for kings to march, prince, yet I do not see Sugriva or any such effort.
ramayana-4-29-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-32.translation: The four months of rain have passed like a hundred years for me, burning with grief, not seeing Sita, gentle one.
ramayana-4-29-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-33.translation: King Sugriva shows no pity for me, Lakshmana, though I am without my beloved, in pain, robbed of my kingdom and exiled.
ramayana-4-29-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-34.translation: Thinking: He is helpless, robbed of his kingdom, insulted by Ravana, wretched, far from home, longing, and has come to me for refuge.
ramayana-4-29-34.meaning: Rama imagines how Sugriva sees him.
ramayana-4-29-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-35.translation: For these reasons, gentle one, I am slighted by the wicked monkey king Sugriva, scorcher of foes.
ramayana-4-29-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-36.translation: Having fixed the time for the search for Sita and made a pact, now that he has what he wants, the fool does not remember.
ramayana-4-29-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-37.translation: Go into Kishkindha and tell Sugriva, that foolish monkey attached to vulgar pleasures, from me:
ramayana-4-29-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-38.translation: Whoever raises the hopes of those who come asking, especially of those who helped him first, and then destroys them, is the lowest of men in the world.
ramayana-4-29-38.meaning: Breaking promises to friends is base.
ramayana-4-29-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-39.translation: Whoever holds to the word he has spoken with truth, whether it turns out good or bad, is a hero and the best of men.
ramayana-4-29-39.meaning: Keeping one's word makes one great.
ramayana-4-29-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-40.translation: Those who, having got what they want, do not help friends who have not, are ungrateful. Even flesh-eaters will not eat them when they are dead.
ramayana-4-29-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-41.translation: Surely he wants to see again my gold-backed bow drawn in battle, flashing like a mass of lightning.
ramayana-4-29-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-42.translation: He wants to hear again the terrible twang of my bowstring in battle when I am angry, like the crash of a thunderbolt.
ramayana-4-29-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-43.translation: Even now, knowing my valour, with you as my ally, hero, I should not have to worry, prince.
ramayana-4-29-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-44.translation: The monkey king, having got what he wanted, does not remember the pact for whose sake this undertaking was made, conqueror of enemy cities.
ramayana-4-29-44.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-45.translation: Having promised the end of the rainy season, the lord of monkeys, enjoying himself, does not notice the four months have passed.
ramayana-4-29-45.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-46.translation: Playing with his ministers and assembly, he does nothing but drink. Sugriva shows no pity for us who are wretched with grief.
ramayana-4-29-46.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-47.translation: Go, mighty child, and speak to Sugriva. Tell him what my anger looks like, and say these words:
ramayana-4-29-47.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-48.translation: The road Vali took when he was killed has not closed. Keep to your pact, Sugriva. Do not follow Vali's path.
ramayana-4-29-48.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-49.translation: Vali alone was killed by my arrow in battle. But you, if you stray from truth, I will kill with your kin.
ramayana-4-29-49.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-50.translation: So, best of men, now that the task is set, say whatever is best. Hurry, the time is passing.
ramayana-4-29-50.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-51.translation: Keep the promise you made me, lord of monkeys, mindful of eternal dharma, or today you may follow Vali to Yama's realm, driven by my arrows.
ramayana-4-29-51.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-29-52.translation: Seeing his elder brother in fierce, swelling anger and lamenting wretchedly, fiery Lakshmana made a fierce resolve about the monkey king.
ramayana-4-29-52.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 29: seeing the clear autumn sky, Rama grieves for Sita and sends Lakshmana to warn Sugriva about his broken promise.

ramayana-4-30-1.translation: Rama's younger brother, undaunted in spirit, spoke to his elder brother, son of a king, who was longing, wretched, stricken with grief and swelling with anger:
ramayana-4-30-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-2.translation: The monkey will not keep to good conduct, will not think of the results of his duties, and will not enjoy the monkey kingdom's fortune, for his mind does not go that way.
ramayana-4-30-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-3.translation: His judgement gone, attached to vulgar pleasures, with no thought of repaying your kindness, let him be killed and see his brother Vali. A kingdom should not be given to one so worthless.
ramayana-4-30-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-4.translation: I cannot hold back this rising anger. I will kill lying Sugriva today. Let Vali's son with the monkey heroes search for the king's wife.
ramayana-4-30-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-5.translation: As he rose, bow in hand, his purpose declared and fierce in battle-anger, Rama, slayer of enemy heroes, spoke to him with careful and soothing words:
ramayana-4-30-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-6.translation: One like you in the world should not do such a wrong. A hero who overcomes wrong through nobility is the best of men.
ramayana-4-30-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-7.translation: You, so good in conduct, should not take this view today, Lakshmana. Keep to the old affection and the friendship made before.
ramayana-4-30-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-8.translation: Avoiding harsh words, speaking conciliating words, you should tell Sugriva that the appointed time has passed.
ramayana-4-30-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-9.translation: Instructed properly by his elder brother, heroic Lakshmana, bull among men and slayer of enemy heroes, entered the city.
ramayana-4-30-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-10.translation: Then wise, good-minded Lakshmana, devoted to his brother's welfare, went angrily to the monkey's palace.
ramayana-4-30-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-11.translation: Holding a bow like Indra's rainbow, he looked like Death at the end of time, like Mount Mandara with its ridges and a mountain peak.
ramayana-4-30-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-12.translation: Doing as he was told, and thinking over his words and the replies to them, Rama's brother, equal to Brihaspati in wisdom, went on.
ramayana-4-30-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-13.translation: Filled with the fire of his brother's anger born of longing and wrath, Lakshmana went on, displeased like a storm wind.
ramayana-4-30-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-14.translation: Forcefully knocking down many sal, palm and ashvakarna trees, hurling aside mountain peaks and other trees as he went,
ramayana-4-30-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-15.translation: smashing rocks with his feet like a swift elephant, taking long strides, he hurried on because of his task.
ramayana-4-30-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-16.translation: The tiger of the Ikshvakus saw the great city of the monkey king, Kishkindha, crowded with troops and hard to reach in a mountain gorge.
ramayana-4-30-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-17.translation: His lips trembling with anger at Sugriva, Lakshmana saw the fearsome monkeys moving outside Kishkindha.
ramayana-4-30-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-18.translation: The monkeys, huge as elephants, seized hundreds of mountain peaks and tall trees in the mountain valley.
ramayana-4-30-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-19.translation: Seeing the monkeys holding weapons, Lakshmana grew twice as angry, like a fire with much fuel.
ramayana-4-30-19.meaning: Their show of force angers him more.
ramayana-4-30-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-20.translation: Seeing him angry, like Death at the end of an age, the monkeys, their limbs gripped by fear, fled by hundreds in all directions.
ramayana-4-30-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-21.translation: Then the chief monkeys entered Sugriva's palace and reported Lakshmana's anger and arrival.
ramayana-4-30-21.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-22.translation: The lustful monkey king, absorbed with Tara in private, did not hear the words of those monkey heroes.
ramayana-4-30-22.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-23.translation: Then, at the ministers' command, the hair-raising monkeys, like mountains, elephants and clouds, went out of the city.
ramayana-4-30-23.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-24.translation: Armed with nails and fangs, fearsome and grotesque in look, all proud as tigers and with fierce faces,
ramayana-4-30-24.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-25.translation: some had the strength of ten elephants, some ten times more, some equal in might to a thousand elephants.
ramayana-4-30-25.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-26.translation: Angry Lakshmana saw all of Kishkindha, hard to approach, filled with mighty monkeys holding trees in their hands.
ramayana-4-30-26.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-27.translation: Then all the monkeys came out from between the wall and the moat and stood openly, spirited.
ramayana-4-30-27.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-28.translation: Knowing Sugriva's negligence and his elder brother's pain, the self-possessed hero, overcome by anger, went on again.
ramayana-4-30-28.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-29.translation: Breathing long, hot, heavy breaths, his eyes red with anger, the tiger among men was like a fire with smoke.
ramayana-4-30-29.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-30.translation: With arrows for his flickering tongue and his bow for his coils, a mass of the venom of his own fire, he was like a five-headed serpent.
ramayana-4-30-30.meaning: He looks like a cobra ready to strike.
ramayana-4-30-30.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-31.translation: Coming upon him, blazing like the fire of doom and angry as a serpent king, Angada fell into deep dismay from fear.
ramayana-4-30-31.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-32.translation: The famous one, his eyes red with rage, instructed Angada: Let Sugriva be told of my arrival, child.
ramayana-4-30-32.meaning: Lakshmana sends Angada with a message.
ramayana-4-30-32.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-33.translation: Say: Rama's younger brother Lakshmana, subduer of enemies, has come to you, troubled by his brother's distress, and stands at the gate.
ramayana-4-30-33.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-34.translation: Hearing Lakshmana's words, grief-stricken Angada went to his uncle and said: Lakshmana has come.
ramayana-4-30-34.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-35.translation: Seeing Lakshmana like a great flood and with a voice like a thunderbolt, the monkeys near him all roared a lion's roar together.
ramayana-4-30-35.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-36.translation: At that great sound the monkey woke, his eyes red and unsteady with drink, his garlands and ornaments in disarray.
ramayana-4-30-36.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-37.translation: Then, hearing Angada's words and coming with him, two ministers of the monkey king, respected and far-sighted,
ramayana-4-30-37.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-38.translation: Plaksha and Prabhava, ministers for policy and dharma, told him of Lakshmana's arrival, to speak of matters high and low.
ramayana-4-30-38.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-39.translation: Having calmed Sugriva with words settled in conciliation, they sat by him as the Maruts by Indra.
ramayana-4-30-39.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-40.translation: The two brothers Rama and Lakshmana, true to their word and noble, have become your friends, worthy of kingship and givers of kingship.
ramayana-4-30-40.meaning: They remind Sugriva who his friends are.
ramayana-4-30-40.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-41.translation: One of them, Lakshmana, bow in hand, stands at the gate. The monkeys tremble in fear of him and cry out.
ramayana-4-30-41.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-42.translation: This Lakshmana, Raghava's brother, with words as his charioteer and resolve as his chariot, has come at Rama's command.
ramayana-4-30-42.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-30-43.translation: Bow your head to him with your son and kin, king. Keep to your pact and be true to your promise.
ramayana-4-30-43.meaning: They urge Sugriva to keep faith.
ramayana-4-30-43.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 30: Rama calms Lakshmana's anger and asks him to speak gently; Lakshmana goes to Kishkindha, and the monkeys warn Sugriva.

ramayana-4-31-1.translation: Hearing Angada's words and that Lakshmana was angry, self-possessed Sugriva and his ministers rose from their seats.
ramayana-4-31-1.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry and consults his ministers.

ramayana-4-31-2.translation: Skilled in counsel and settled in deliberation, having weighed what was serious and what was slight, he spoke to his ministers who knew counsel:
ramayana-4-31-2.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry and consults his ministers.

ramayana-4-31-3.translation: I have said nothing wrong and done nothing wrong. I wonder why Lakshmana, Raghava's brother, is angry.
ramayana-4-31-3.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry and consults his ministers.

ramayana-4-31-4.translation: Unfriendly enemies of mine, always looking for weak points, must have told Raghava's brother of faults I do not have.
ramayana-4-31-4.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry and consults his ministers.

ramayana-4-31-5.translation: Here, all of you, use your judgement properly and find out carefully and slowly what he intends.
ramayana-4-31-5.meaning: He asks his ministers to find out.
ramayana-4-31-5.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry and consults his ministers.

ramayana-4-31-6.translation: I have no fear of Lakshmana or Raghava. But a friend angered without cause does cause alarm.
ramayana-4-31-6.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry and consults his ministers.

ramayana-4-31-7.translation: Making a friend is easy in every way; keeping one is hard. Because minds are changeable, affection breaks over even a little thing.
ramayana-4-31-7.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-8.translation: That is why I am afraid of great Rama, for I cannot repay the help he gave me.
ramayana-4-31-8.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-9.translation: When Sugriva said this, Hanuman, chief of monkeys, spoke his own reasoning among the monkey ministers.
ramayana-4-31-9.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-10.translation: It is no wonder at all, lord of the monkey hosts, that you do not forget the loving, good help you received.
ramayana-4-31-10.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-11.translation: For your sake heroic Raghava, casting fear far away, killed Vali, equal to Indra in valour.
ramayana-4-31-11.meaning: Rama took great risks for Sugriva.
ramayana-4-31-11.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-12.translation: No doubt Raghava is angry out of affection. He has sent his brother Lakshmana, who increases fortune.
ramayana-4-31-12.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-13.translation: Careless, you do not see the time, best of those who know time. The lovely autumn has begun, dark with blooming saptachchada trees.
ramayana-4-31-13.meaning: Autumn has come and gone unnoticed.
ramayana-4-31-13.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-14.translation: The sky is clear of clouds, the planets and stars are bright, and all directions, rivers and lakes are clear.
ramayana-4-31-14.meaning: The season to march is here.
ramayana-4-31-14.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-15.translation: You do not know that the time for action has come, chief of monkeys. Clearly you are careless, and so Lakshmana has come here.
ramayana-4-31-15.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-16.translation: You should bear even harsh words from great Raghava, spoken through another, for he is in pain and his wife was taken.
ramayana-4-31-16.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-17.translation: Since you are at fault, I see nothing fitting except to fold your hands and win Lakshmana's goodwill.
ramayana-4-31-17.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-18.translation: Ministers appointed must surely tell the king what is good. So, putting fear aside, I speak firm words.
ramayana-4-31-18.meaning: Hanuman speaks frankly as his duty.
ramayana-4-31-18.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-19.translation: When angered, Raghava, lifting his bow, could bring the whole world with gods, asuras and gandharvas under his control.
ramayana-4-31-19.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-20.translation: One whom you must win back later is not one to anger, especially for a grateful person who remembers past help.
ramayana-4-31-20.meaning: Do not anger those you depend on.
ramayana-4-31-20.explanation: Kishkindha Kanda, chapter 31: Sugriva wonders why Lakshmana is angry; Hanuman tells him plainly that he has let the agreed time pass.

ramayana-4-31-21.translation: Bow your head to him with your son and friends, king, and keep to your pact, under his will as a wife under her husband's.
